candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 37 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 38 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of disseminated coccidioidomycosis should 125 consider the following regarding trial population: 126

• Trial entry criteria should include a diagnosis of disseminated coccidioidomycosis based 140 on typical symptoms and radiographic abnormalities, with enzyme immunoassay and 141 immunodiffusion or complement fixation (CF) testing to detect immunoglobulin M and 142 immunoglobulin G antibodies. The diagnosis of disseminated coccidioidomycosis should 143 be confirmed based on the presence of C. immitis or C. posadasii in culture of bone, joint 144 or tissue lesions, sputum, bronchial wash, or lung tissue or pleural fluid, or identification 145 of endosporulating spherules in histological preparations. 146
candidates.context: • Different disseminated coccidioidomycosis patient populations (e.g., nonmeningeal 148 coccidioidomycosis versus coccidioidal meningitis) may have different disease 149 manifestations and different responses to treatment and may require different trial 150 endpoints. 151

candidates.statement: – Sponsors should consider whether phase 3 trials should limit enrollment based on 153 patient characteristics such as disease form (nonmeningeal coccidioidomycosis versus 154 coccidioidal meningitis), treatment experience (naïve versus refractory), and 155 comorbidities. 156

candidates.statement: Phase 3 trials evaluating new drugs for the treatment of disseminated coccidioidomycosis should 168 generally have a clinical endpoint as the primary endpoint, with a microbiological endpoint as a 169 key secondary endpoint. As disseminated coccidioidomycosis is a heterogeneous disease, 170 endpoints should represent the outcomes that are most meaningful to the target population, can 171 be improved with treatment, and are expected to be sensitive to detect a treatment effect. 172 Sponsors should consider the following regarding efficacy endpoints: 173

• Primary efficacy endpoints should be based on COAs, such as a patient-reported outcome 177 (PRO) instrument assessing symptoms of disseminated coccidioidomycosis. Sponsors 178 should discuss with the Division other appropriate COAs that could be used, such as 179 observer-reported outcomes, clinician-reported outcomes, and performance outcomes. In 180 addition to use in the primary efficacy endpoint, COAs may also be appropriate for use in 181 secondary endpoints. 182
candidates.context: • Currently, FDA is not aware of any specific PRO instruments that have been 184 demonstrated to be fit-for-purpose 8 to assess symptoms of disseminated 185 coccidioidomycosis to support regulatory decision-making and medical product labeling. 186 Sponsors should discuss with the Division existing, new, or modified PRO instruments 187 for this use. 188

The 219 process to construct a personalized endpoint should be standardized, and the criteria 220 for selecting the outcome assessments should be consistent across sites and patients. 221 The same set of outcome assessments should be assessed for all patients, regardless of 222 their own personalized endpoint, to allow for an assessment of any new or worsening 223 symptoms and/or functional limitations during the trial. Personalized endpoint 224 methods and determination of which symptom or symptoms would be a part of this 225 personalized endpoint approach should be discussed with the Division early in the 226 drug development process. For further information on a personalized endpoint 227 approach, please refer to the draft guidance for industry Patient-Focused Drug 228 Development: Incorporating Clinical Outcome Assessments Into Endpoints For 229 Regulatory Decision-Making (April 2023). 14
candidates.context: 13 See the Duke-Margolis Center for Health Policy’s Developing Personalized Clinical Outcome Assessments, available at https://healthpolicy.duke.edu/sites/default/files/2020-03/meeting_summary_4_5_17.pdf . – An appropriate endpoint could be the time to sustained symptom alleviation or 232 resolution assessed over an appropriate duration. Sustained symptom alleviation or 233 resolution can be defined as occurring when no key disseminated 234 coccidioidomycosis-related symptom scored higher than a prespecified threshold over 235 a clinically meaningful time period (as documented using a PRO instrument). 236

candidates.statement: – Based on the role of the PRO instrument and data obtained during its development, 244 establishing a range of a priori thresholds (i.e., the change in the individual PRO 245 score over a predetermined time period that should be interpreted as a clinically 246 meaningful within-patient change) is useful when considering options for the primary 247 endpoint. A variety of primary endpoint options are appropriate. For example, if a 248 total symptom score can be computed for the PRO, possible endpoints might include 249 time to sustained resolution of symptoms or meeting a prespecified extent of 250 clinically meaningful improvement. Sponsors should discuss endpoints with the 251 Division. 252
candidates.context: – Piloting the proposed PRO instrument in early clinical studies provides an 238 opportunity to evaluate the instrument’s measurement properties (reliability, validity, 239 and ability to detect change), to evaluate clinically meaningful within-patient change 240 in scores (using methods such as anchor-based methods), and to confirm the endpoint 241 definition before use in phase 3 trials. 15 – The timing and frequency of the primary endpoint assessment and duration of follow- 254 up will depend on the nature of the chosen trial population and treatment effect of the 255 drug or drugs. Given the protracted nature of disseminated coccidioidal infections, the 256 primary outcome assessment should be performed after at least 6 to 12 months of 257 study drug treatment. Sponsors should prospectively discuss these issues with the 258 Division. 259

candidates.statement: • Microbiological endpoints, such as negative cultures or decline in CF titers could be 263 included as secondary endpoints. Serial monitoring of serum CF titers to Coccidioides 264 species should be performed every 1 to 3 months for at least 1 year. A decline (≥2 265 dilution reduction) in quantitative CF titers measured at a central laboratory over the 266 duration of the trial or at months 6 or 12 could serve as a secondary endpoint. 267
